title: Tenure
description: One person's turn at one office. A kind of its own and not a relation, because a relation's id is from--to--type and one person may hold one office three times (plan review, finding 1); the id is therefore a free slug, `soares-prime-minister-1976`. Two tenures of one office may overlap — a regency is not a mistake and a year is the finest bound this model has — so nothing here refuses that.

sources.description: A tenure asserts that this person held this office in these years, which is an argument like an edge's: it cites at least one source (rule 6).

person.description: The actor who held the office. An actor of type person, and rule 26 says so — a party does not hold a presidency.

office.description: The office record this is a turn at (rule 26).

when.description: How long they held it. end: null means they still do. It must overlap the office's own interval where the office has one (rule 26).

startedBy.description: Optional: the event that began this tenure — the election, the coup, the succession. It resolves to an event under rule 3 and may not name a tombstone (rule 11), and it is how a result that changed a government stays connected to the atlas without an invented edge (plan decision 3).

note.description: Optional, short, and written by a person: what the office, the person and two dates cannot say — that they were the founding secretary-general, or that the end is the year they left on being elected President. Carried in the topology exactly as a relation's is, because a tenure has no card of its own and is drawn from the office's.
